headline: Prioritize playback reliability: fix stops/skips and crashes before expanding policy or interface work.
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation
Prioritize **playback**, first addressing `playback.playback_stops_or_skips` and `playback.crash_freeze`. These are defects in core playback reliability; focus effort on diagnosing and preventing unintended stops, song changes, freezes, and crashes.

## Evidence
`playback.playback_stops_or_skips` has 19,469 complaints [C013] and severity sum 61,848 [C014]. `playback.crash_freeze` has 8,299 complaints [C025], severity sum 29,991 [C026], and mean severity 3.613809 [C027]. Playback’s sev4+ share is 26.54% [A021], indicating a high-severity concentration. Playback’s share of reviews shrank from 8.11% early [T033] to 4.55% late [T036], so this is not a growing-share area; its severity still supports focused reliability work. Representative reports: `cf91b556-b439-4e37-8eb1-0b79608282f5`, `d5cf4d6e-34b7-4e12-bf8d-995d4e09503f`, and `b007bb8d-f5e0-4b61-9575-e03bc1f755aa`.

## Alternatives considered
The leading issue is `billing.premium_paywall`, with 49,834 complaints [C001] and severity sum 141,749 [C002]. Its scale makes it important, but it principally reflects a deliberate free-tier restriction and subscription policy, not a playback defect; I would address it through policy and expectation-setting work rather than make it the next quarter’s primary reliability investment. The second-ranked `other.general` issue has 66,259 complaints [C005], but generic privacy/data concerns are non-actionable context here, not a product area. Billing/support’s share grew from 3.92% [T009] to 13.04% [T012], and usability’s from 10.98% [T039] to 12.92% [T042]; both merit attention, but the leading usability concerns include ads and interface changes, which call for policy/design decisions rather than fixing broken playback. Access also grew, from 0.99% [T003] to 1.83% [T006], but has a smaller overall complaint share of 3.33% [A039].

## Limitations
These are self-selected public reviews, not a customer-population measure. Cancellation records express intent, not observed churn. Trend windows exclude partial first and last months. Review classifications may leave defects and policy complaints unresolved or mixed.
